correctness.rationale: For every m>=1, n=2m+1, the regular integral path complex has allowed arcs e_(i,a), 1<=a<=m. For 2<=a<=m the permitted 2-path (i,i+1,i+a) has entirely allowed boundary e_(i+1,a-1)-e_(i,a)+e_(i,1). Iterating expresses any closed 1-chain modulo boundaries as a chain of unit arcs. A closed unit-arc chain has constant integer coefficient, hence H1 is cyclic generated by h=sum_i (i,i+1). Define W on every regular ordered pair (u,v), u!=v, as positive residue of v-u modulo n. For an allowed elementary 2-path its positive increments a,b satisfy a+b<=2m<n; thus W(boundary)=b-(a+b)+a=0, including every Omega2 boundary by restriction. W(h)=n!=0; h has infinite order and H1=Z. The edge formula should formally be understood as equivalence of 1-chains modulo B1, rather than [e] for a non-cycle. All quantified boundaries and m=1 checked. Independent finite identity tests (m=1..12) confirmed exact chord reductions, tournament orientation and W cancellation; no finite check substitutes for the argument.

originality.rationale: Direct decisive prior coverage: Tang–Yau arXiv:2602.04140v2 dated 2026-10-09, preceding this 2026-10-11 research record, proves in Theorem 3.15 that for every field K and n>2d the regular path homology of interval-step circulant digraph C_n^{1,...,d} has H1=K, higher H>=2 zero, and the unit-step Hamiltonian cycle generates H1. Set d=m and n=2m+1; the assigned R_n is precisely this digraph. Since the finite integer path-chain complex has finitely generated homology and H0(Z)=Z, the universal coefficient theorem gives dim_Q H1(Q)=rank H1(Z)=1 and dim_Fp H1(Fp)=rank+number of p-primary cyclic factors in H1(Z), so all-field dimension 1 excludes torsion for every prime; H1(Z)=Z. Remark 3.16 explicitly maps each arc of length s to its consecutive unit-arc chain, precisely the assigned stronger description. The submitted winding form is an alternative proof of a covered theorem, not a novel theorem. This is more than a failed search or title similarity.
